name: Calvek Hibiscus-Pomelo Blaze
description: A sharp, high-acid soda combining synth-hibiscus and synth-pomelo in a vivid crimson-pink drink with aggressive carbonation. Strathmore positions it as an energy-adjacent product without the energy drink branding.
flavor_profile: Bright, almost aggressive hibiscus tartness cut with the bitter pith of pomelo, heavy carbonation, dry finish
cultural_context: Calvek is the drink of choice at Shelf night markets and informal event spaces — the vivid color photographs well even on cheap devices, giving it a social presence disproportionate to its rank. Strathmore has never invested significantly in marketing it, letting the aesthetics do the work.
story_hooks: Calvek's vivid crimson color comes from a synth-dye compound that is one regulatory review away from being banned — Strathmore knows, and has been lobbying quietly to delay the review.
A specific underground music event in the Shelf has become so associated with Calvek that the drink is now used as informal entry currency — and someone is counterfeiting the cans.

A Tier 5 mixologist published a viral piece declaring Calvek 'the most honest drink in GLMZ' — the sudden Tier 4 interest is disrupting the Shelf supply chain and pricing out the people who actually drink it.
